item.title: US judge strikes down policy suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 nations
item.description:
By Kanishka Singh and Nate Raymond

WASHINGTON, Aug 21 (Reuters) - A U.S. judge on Friday struck down a Trump administration policy suspending the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, saying that the policy exceeded Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statutory authority.

item.title: Trump says Iran not ready to make the 'right deal'
item.description:
By Kanishka Singh and Ismail Shakil

WASHINGTON, Aug 21 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday he thought Tehran was not ready to make the "right deal" and that Washington was observing "what happens" in the Iran war.

QUOTES AND DETAILS:

• "It just means that we're seeing what happens," Trump told reporters when asked if U.S. military options with Iran were limited.

• Washington pledged this week to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership.

item.title: Turkey to seek Interpol notice for Netanyahu in Gaza flotilla case
item.description: ISTANBUL, Aug 21 (Reuters) - Turkey said on Friday it would seek an Interpol red notice for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as part of a domestic criminal case linked to an attack on activists seeking to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza.

item.title: NATO members discuss Strait of Hormuz options without alliance involvement
item.description: BRUSSELS, Aug 21 (Reuters) - NATO's top commander convened a videoconference earlier this week to facilitate possible contributions to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, his spokesperson told Reuters, adding that this is not a NATO mission.

item.title: UK, Canada, Australia slam Israel ending probe into aid worker killings
item.description:
Britain, Canada, and Australia on Friday condemned as "shameful" Israel's decision to close an investigation into the death of seven aid workers killed in Gaza in 2024.

The World Central Kitchen employees -- three Britons, a dual US-Canadian national, a Pole, an Australian, and a Palestinian -- died in a drone strike on their vehicle convoy after overseeing the unloading of a food aid shipment.

Israel's military called the incident a "tragic mistake".
